subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Ocean Liner Era
description: One-minute skill: The Ocean Liner Era.

hook.text: Before airplanes, crossing the ocean meant boarding a ship. Millions traveled this way every year.

buildup.text: Ocean liners competed on speed, luxury, and size. The Blue Riband went to the fastest Atlantic crossing.

discovery.text: Titanic, Lusitania, Queen Mary—these ships were floating cities with ballrooms, pools, and class divisions.

twist.text: Jet airliners killed the industry in the 1960s. A five-day crossing couldn't compete with a six-hour flight.

climax.text: Ocean liners survive only as cruise ships—selling the voyage itself, not the destination.

punchline.text: The journey became the product when the destination got easier.

quiz.question: What killed the ocean liner industry?
options: Jet airliners offering faster Atlantic crossings
